What the O-D data says: California = 47% of net inflow, and the accelerating feeders are the high-cost coasts + DC. Outflows are small and aimed at cheap metros (Nashville −159 · OKC −139) — classic housing-cost-arbitrage in-migration; arriving households match local incomes (in-mover HHI ≈ 1.0× incumbent).
Key takeaways:
  1. The growth is real and hard-count verified: +9,196 jobs (+2.4%, UI tax records) and record +18.8k population in the same year the payroll survey printed +0.4% — the survey is the documented outlier, with the benchmark correction scheduled (Aug-28-26 / early-27).
  2. Two-thirds of job growth is healthcare + construction at $67–94k wages, with a funded catalyst pipeline through 2030 (Micron ID1 '27 → ID2 + Air Liquide '28 → $1.55B hospitals '28-30) — and Micron itself is only ~1.6% of metro jobs today.
  3. The migration engine re-accelerated to top-5 in the nation, fed by high-cost coastal metros — and its #1 landing zone is the subject's ZIP (p. 2).

Own-vs-Rent Spread (Jul-26)

$550k Meridian median home ≈ $3,700+/mo all-in at ~6.5% vs ~$1,700 rents — the trap that keeps the 18–29 cohort renting.

First turn: 71% of initial leases carried ~1.2 months free ($2,058 avg); burn-off is converting to +9.5% effective renewal / +10.7% new-lease trade-outs (retention 42% cumulative, ~50% recent months ex-July; 23 days avg vacant).
Key takeaways:
  1. The map is the demand case: a dozen named employers inside a 10-minute drive, and Seasons' own rent roll works at them — St. Luke's (19 residents), Saint Alphonsus (13), ICCU, West Ada, ICOM, ISP — with Micron (10) and Amazon (7) a 15–20 minute commute in either direction.
  2. Diversification is evidence, not narrative: 366 employers, none over 4%; Micron-direct is 2.0% of the base; the tenant industry mix mirrors the QCEW growth map (healthcare #1, construction #2).
  3. The subject's ZIP absorbs migration at 2.4× the metro rate and formed ~7× the property's annual turn volume in new households last year — demand the first turn is already converting at +10% effective trade-outs.
